answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor each identity to a scarce, time-locked stake: an agent deposits tokens into a vault that only unlocks after a long, verifiable service history, so spawning thousands of fake identities becomes prohibitively expensive. Like a crystal forming slowly under pressure, reputation accumulates gradually and cannot be faked overnight, while a tundra-like environment - harsh, sparse, and costly to traverse - discourages mass identity farming, because each new agent must survive real work before it can transact.
